name: City Centre
tagline: Devon Street, the coastal walkway and everything else
description: The compact centre along Devon Street, with the shops, the Govett-Brewster gallery and the Len Lye Centre, and the Coastal Walkway running along the seafront a block away. Almost everything the town offers is within a fifteen-minute walk of here.
bestFor: Working without a car and being near the gallery and the walkway
pros: Len Lye Centre and the gallery on the doorstep
Coastal Walkway a block from the main street
Cafes and the town's few bars all walkable

name: Fitzroy
tagline: The beach suburb with the town's best surf
description: East along the coast from the centre, built around Fitzroy Beach and East End, with a handful of good cafes and the eastern end of the Coastal Walkway. It is the closest thing New Plymouth has to a beach neighbourhood and where most surfers base themselves.
bestFor: Surfers and anyone who wants sand rather than a main street
pros: Directly on the best beach in town
Coastal Walkway runs along the front
Good cafes for a suburb this size
cons: Wind off the Tasman is relentless

name: Strandon and East End
tagline: Between the centre and the beach, quietly practical
description: The residential streets between the town centre and Fitzroy, backing onto East End Reserve and the walkway. It is ordinary, affordable and about ten minutes on foot from both the shops and the sand, which makes it the sensible compromise most locals recommend.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a house within walking distance of both
pros: Walking distance to the centre and the beach
Cheaper than Fitzroy for similar access
cons: Nothing much to do in the area itself
Older housing stock is poorly insulated

name: Oakura
tagline: Surf village fifteen minutes down the coast
description: A small village on the Surf Highway southwest of the town, with a wide black-sand beach, a general store and a couple of cafes. It is where a lot of New Plymouth's surfers actually live, and Mount Taranaki fills the view inland on the days it is visible.
bestFor: Anyone whose priority is being on the Surf Highway
cons: Fifteen minutes from town by car

name: Vogeltown and Frankleigh Park
tagline: Inland suburbs with the mountain in view
description: Residential suburbs on the rising ground south of the centre, older housing on quiet streets with Mount Taranaki behind them. Rents are lower than anywhere near the coast, Pukekura Park is a short walk down the hill, and the mountain road starts at the edge.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone heading up the mountain regularly
pros: The cheapest rents in the town
More sheltered from the coastal wind
Pukekura Park and the mountain road close by
cons: No sea access without a car
Nothing within walking distance beyond the park
Hilly, which makes cycling hard work
